per_scene.scene: Weather and time of day (B, C, E)
per_scene.assessment: Time of day is G2's strongest system: noon, golden hour and dusk read convincingly on B and E (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-civDemo/54b82655-610f-500e-a185-8fae64bdd108/scratchpad/m7gfx2/captures/scenes/sheets/scenes-hours.jpg). Weather works but is thin. Rain reads mainly as a grey grade, puddles read as grey concrete patches between tufts, streaks are barely visible at 1080p, and buttercups are flat yellow dots (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-civDemo/54b82655-610f-500e-a185-8fae64bdd108/scratchpad/m7gfx2/captures/scenes/g2/b-rain/bench-b-front.png; crops brain-front-mid.jpg, brain-front-ground.jpg). Mist sits nicely in the valleys (e-mist). Caveat: every still is an 8-sample accumulated frame on llvmpipe, which hides temporal aliasing, so the thatch and grass moire will crawl in motion. No number here is performance evidence (llvmpipe, not Victus evidence).

G2 is an enormous step from G1 on every sheet. Geometry, PBR materials, sky, cascaded shadows, AO and the time of day are past the San Andreas floor. But ranks 1-3 below are glaring artefacts: the sand-dune/felt meadow, fingerprint shadow acne, and the clone-army crowd. C's golden showcase, D's close beats and E's settlements are not clearly above the bar. Nothing here is production quality. Most top fixes are presentation-only shader and tuning work. Ranks 1 and 2 will move the earlier stages' frames, so the weather-off identity check should be re-baselined deliberately rather than used as a reason to keep the artefacts.

top_issues.issue: The meadow terrain is flat felt beyond the ground-cover reach, ends on a hard cover edge, and turns sand-beige under a low sun (the golden-hour battlefield reads as desert dunes).
top_issues.evidence: C golden hour: the same terrain measures mid-meadow RGB 162,135,82 at hue 40 deg against hue 72-76 deg at noon; the noon albedo itself is a desaturated olive (hue 75 deg, sat 0.36) (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-civDemo/54b82655-610f-500e-a185-8fae64bdd108/scratchpad/m7gfx2/captures/scenes/g2/c/bench-c-vista-golden.png, bench-c-clash-golden.png; crop /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-civDemo/54b82655-610f-500e-a185-8fae64bdd108/scratchpad/critic-g2-iter1/crops/c-vg-sand.jpg). Flatness and the hard edge: 24-px local luminance std is 0.6-1.8 beyond the cover against 8-28 inside it; in B wide-noon it jumps from 1.8 to 25.0 within 30 px (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-civDemo/54b82655-610f-500e-a185-8fae64bdd108/scratchpad/m7gfx2/captures/scenes/g2/b/bench-b-wide-noon.png; crop /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-civDemo/54b82655-610f-500e-a185-8fae64bdd108/scratchpad/critic-g2-iter1/crops/b-wn-boundary.jpg). E's noon foreground is flat (std 0.6-2.3) from y=600 to the frame bottom (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-civDemo/54b82655-610f-500e-a185-8fae64bdd108/scratchpad/m7gfx2/captures/scenes/g2/e/bench-e-vista-noon.png). The stage report section 10 confirms that haze=1 and aerial=0 do not remove the beige.
top_issues.fix: Fix it in the terrain material and ground-cover system, not with haze. (a) Retint the meadow albedo greener and more saturated (target about hue 85-95 deg, sat about 0.5 at noon) so a 9-deg sun lands on gold-green rather than tan. (b) Add low-frequency macro variation in the terrain shader: 2-3 grass tones, dry and trampled patches and worn tracks from world-space noise at 20-200 m scale, plus a detail normal. (c) Fade cover density stochastically over the last third of its range, and tint the ground under and beyond it to the cards' average colour so no edge remains. (d) Add a cheap far-grass LOD (sparse card clusters or 2-3 shell layers to about 150 m). (e) Drop golden-hour haze from 3. Re-baseline the weather-off identity deliberately, then re-capture C vista/clash golden, B wide noon and E vista noon.

top_issues.issue: Cascaded-shadow acne draws concentric fingerprint or contour rings on smooth sunlit slopes at golden hour.

Stage report section 10: it is absent with the single shadow map; the cascades use a constant 1.6-texel depth bias and a normal offset sized by cascade 0's texel.
top_issues.fix: In CascadedShadowMap, replace the constant bias with a slope-scaled bias (bias = c0 + c1*tan(acos(N.L)), clamped), and size the normal offset per cascade by that cascade's own world texel size; optionally add receiver-plane depth bias. This is a few lines. Add a grazing-light test that counts acne pixels on a smooth lit slope, then re-capture C rout, C golden vistas and D field.

(e) Correct the CMU-retarget head/neck pitch, or add an additive look-at toward the enemy line, so heads come up. For the authored hoplite guard in A, author at least two pose variants plus phase offsets. The crowd already blends two clips from bone textures, so this is a per-instance uniform plus a small table. per_scene.assessment: Clearly above the San Andreas bar in geometry, materials and lighting, and the biggest step from G1 (capsules to people). Good: the hero aspis (embossed rim, worn bronze) holds up full-frame in 'kit'; 'line' reads as a period hoplite file with varied shield heights; eyes with catchlights, beard fur shells and the grim to battle-cry expression read; the magenta skin bands are gone. Broken or placeholder: grey scalp hair renders over the background hoplite's closed Corinthian helmet (brow and eye openings) in 3 of 7 stills: battlecry, two-shot and two-shot-golden (rank 1, glaring). At the closest framings the faces are still game faces: faceted cheek and jaw silhouette, painted dotted brows and lashes (rank 10). The hero soldier's face inside the helmet is lit as if in open air, so it looks pasted behind the bronze. The commander-grim framing parks his head on the shield rim. The cuirass edge goes jagged under the raised arm in battlecry, and the greaves read as matte beige rather than bronze in 'line'. Detail is above the bar, but the scene is not clean.

Above the bar. Two opposing forces stand in readable blocks with standards and officers, forest, village and river behind, under convincing low-sun shadows. The pose variants removed the clone look, and front-rank faces and kit read in 'front'. Placeholder or broken: the sky is a cloudless gradient (17-25 % of front and between). The river is a straight spillway with colourless near-white banks directly behind the red force in all three wide shots and rear-high (rank 4). The village is a toy ring of identical cone huts. The backlit ground cover in 'standard' is neon lime (rank 5). Mid-distance crowd faces have glowing white eyes and grey-blue mask-like beards (rank 9). Open-palm grips leave some spears floating. The noon horizon is a crisp line under thin haze. Rain and mist work as looks (veiled distance, darker wet meadow, no snow look), but rain has no splashes and the puddles are flat grey.

The scale reads: 2,100 trace-driven soldiers, a legible clash cluster, long golden-hour shadows, and the acne is gone. Measured against the spirit of the bar, though, this is the weakest scene. The field is a pristine meadow with no effects at all after 1,334 s of fighting: no trampling, dust or debris (SceneC uses no SmokeLayer; QM8 C asks for effects) (rank 7). At vista range the armies are coloured dots, like a strategy map. The far land is teal camouflage at noon and desert dunes into the sun (rank 8). 'advance' is 44 % empty sky (rank 2). The only close shot, melee-low, draws its crowd at lod1 (about 3.2k triangles, vertex colour): tunics torn into black stretched shards, untextured faceted helmet bowls, ground-cover flowers drawn through the fallen (rank 6). It is above San Andreas in scale; at close range it is roughly San Andreas-class per character.

The assets are above the bar. The surrender two-shot (raised sword over the kneeling officer) is staged clearly, and commander-against-sky and standards are strong low-angle compositions. As a cinematic, though, it does not yet read as an aftermath. In 01-prisoners the surrendered men hold levelled spears and raised shields, so they read as a spear wall advancing on the camera (rank 3; TraceCrowd.cs:395-402 never touches carried items). 06-fallen is a jumble of armed kneeling men and interpenetrating bodies. On the crane the smoke reads as two white lens smudges, and in the cut-away as dark smudges. 04 and 05 are about 60 % featureless sky. The officer close-up shows a hard-edged grey stubble film and patchwork face shadows (rank 10). A straight-topped brown slab sits in the cut-away's forest gap. Its readability is at or below the reference's cutscenes: it needs staging, not more rendering features.

The strongest scene and clearly above the bar: a forest of real tree models with convincing canopy and light, golden and dusk vistas with warm light on the stronghold, mist banks in the valley, and a high view that lays out village, fields, forest and stronghold legibly. Placeholder: the fortification is a clean model kit, with a flat dark gate void, thin blue sky-reflection lines on the ledge tops and uniform blocks (rank 11). The village is lifeless: no people, animals, hearth smoke or paths. The river is the straight chalk-banked flume, with a zigzag straight-segment waterline and saucer-shaped boulders in the river shot (rank 4). The far land at noon is mottled camouflage (rank 8), and the sky is cloudless. In rain the river turns into a white ribbon.

per_scene.assessment: Clearly above the San Andreas bar. It has real faces with lashes, irises, teeth and an expression change, and crested Corinthian helmets, linen corselets, a lush meadow with poppies and soft golden backlight. The painted, worn bronze aspis with its embossed rim (bench-a-kit) is the best asset in the set. In bench-a-soldier-face the Corinthian helmet reads as chalky beige resin, not bronze: it is flat and reflects nothing of the sky. In bench-a-two-shot the commander is a bare head sitting on top of the aspis. No glaring artefact. Not production quality.

Above the San Andreas bar in scale and lighting: 320 soldiers with shadows, standards, real oak trees, dense ground cover and heaped clouds. Most frames still show a tell. (1) In bench-b-wide-noon, -wide-golden, -wide-dusk and -rear-high the river is a bright white straight channel, like a concrete spillway, with pale grey slabs on the valley sides. (4) The backlit tufts in bench-b-standard are near-white mint plastic. The mist looks are atmospheric. In rain, the wet ground between tufts reads as pale cement. Verdict: above the bar, not clean.

2,100 soldiers with shadows, each one driven by the trace, are far beyond anything San Andreas showed, and bench-c-clash-noon reads as a battle from the air. Two things pull it down.
